name: OH-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -15 point partisan lean
Incumbent Troy Balderson holds a massive fundraising edge ($1.98M cash vs $19K)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at only about 5%
No public polling available for this race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Balderson: a -15 point Republican-leaning district, a two-term incumbent with a roughly 20-to-1 cash advantage, and no signs of a serious Democratic operation on Jerrad Christian's side. Prediction markets agree, pricing Democratic odds near 5%, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of about -16.
model.watch: Any surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a national environment turning sharply against Republicans, would be the first sign this race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Balderson seeks another term in a central Ohio district that leans about 15 points Republican at the presidential level. He enters the general election with roughly $2 million on hand after raising $1.7 million, while Democrat Jerrad Christian has raised under $85,000 with about $19,000 available, leaving a stark resource gap and no evidence of outside groups investing in the race.

No public general-election polls cover the district and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 5% chance. A favorable national climate for Democrats could narrow the margin somewhat, but the combination of district lean, incumbency, and money makes Balderson a clear favorite.
